speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing high blood pressure and if you have any symptoms like headaches, dizziness, or shortness of breath? Also, do you have any family history of hypertension or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since this is an incidental finding in an asymptomatic child, have the blood pressure readings been elevated in all four limbs, and have you noticed any abdominal masses or hearing issues? I would also like to examine the child's abdomen and listen for bruits over the kidneys and carotid arteries.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant finding; does the high blood pressure also affect your right arm when we check the pulse, and do you have any swelling or pain in your left arm or legs? I would also like to feel your neck arteries to compare the pulse strength between your left and right sides.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Blood pressure measurements in all four extremities. REQUEST TEST: Renal artery Doppler ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES. Does the child have any history of weak pulses or coolness in the left arm or legs?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure Right Upper Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Blood Pressure Lower Extremities: Lower than upper extremities (differential noted). Pulses: 2+ radial pulses, trace femoral pulses. Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation; normal left ventricular function. Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, no rib notching. Renal artery Doppler ultrasound and left arm blood pressure/pulse status: Data not available in current records.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results showing a blood pressure differential between the upper and lower extremities, weak femoral pulses, and aortic narrowing on echocardiogram confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.
